hyperedges.label: Broker-driven uninstall flow: broker -> safety -> uninstall -> leftover scan -> backup/quarantine

nodes.label: Deep Uninstall
nodes.rationale: Vendor uninstaller first, then leftover scan scored by confidence and removed with backup; Force remove covers broken/missing uninstallers.

nodes.label: Least Privilege / On-demand Elevated Broker
nodes.rationale: UI runs as standard user; broker started via UAC, reached over ACL'd named pipe, accepts only item IDs; per-user uninstallers run unelevated.

nodes.label: Quarantine, .reg Backups and Undo History
nodes.rationale: Files moved rather than deleted so every removal transaction can be undone; backups purged after 30 days.

nodes.label: Semantic Versioning
nodes.rationale: Single source of truth is [workspace.package].version in root Cargo.toml; crates, Tauri bundle and app/package.json follow it.

nodes.label: Rust + Tauri 2 Technology Choice
nodes.rationale: Small binary, no GC, first-class windows-rs bindings, WebView2 ships with Windows; C#/Electron too heavy, C++ too slow to build UI, Go weak COM.

nodes.label: Slint Alternative UI
nodes.rationale: Swap in if idle RAM must stay under ~30 MB; core crates unchanged since UI is a thin layer.

nodes.label: Process & Privilege Model (one binary, two modes)
nodes.rationale: Non-elevated UI so browsing never needs UAC; snipe.exe --broker relaunched via ShellExecuteEx runas once per session.
nodes.norm_label: process & privilege model (one binary, two modes)

nodes.label: Elevated Broker Named Pipe (DACL to user SID)
nodes.norm_label: elevated broker named pipe (dacl to user sid)

nodes.label: Item-ID-only Broker Requests
nodes.rationale: Broker re-resolves IDs against its own inventory so a compromised UI cannot request deletion of arbitrary paths.

nodes.label: Avoid WMI Win32_Product (use MsiEnumProductsEx)
nodes.rationale: Win32_Product is slow and triggers MSI self-repair on every product.

nodes.label: Incremental Refresh via Collector Fingerprints
nodes.rationale: Re-run a collector only when registry LastWriteTime or dir mtimes change; deferred in favor of JSON snapshot cache.

nodes.label: Inventory Cache (SQLite planned, JSON snapshot implemented)
nodes.norm_label: inventory cache (sqlite planned, json snapshot implemented)

nodes.label: Restart Manager Process Shutdown
nodes.rationale: Planned; implementation uses Toolhelp instead (Restart Manager deferred).

nodes.label: Job Object for Uninstallers
nodes.rationale: Many uninstallers spawn a %TEMP% copy and exit early; job object lets the orchestrator wait for children.

nodes.label: UninstallString Parsing (CommandLineToArgvW, no cmd /c)
nodes.rationale: Prevents command injection; fuzz-tested in hardening phase.

nodes.label: Leftover Confidence Scoring (0-100)
nodes.rationale: >=80 pre-selected, 50-79 shown unchecked, <50 hidden; publisher-only matches penalized to protect shared vendor folders.

nodes.label: Deny-list of Critical Paths and Keys
nodes.rationale: Checked after canonicalization to prevent TOCTOU and .. tricks.
nodes.norm_label: deny-list of critical paths and keys

nodes.label: Install Tracing via ETW
nodes.rationale: Revo-style traced install for exact removal; deferred.

nodes.label: Transaction Journal and Undo
nodes.rationale: Steps recorded before and after execution so operations can resume or roll back after a crash.

nodes.label: Never Follow Reparse Points
nodes.rationale: Delete the link not the target, preventing deletion of C:\ through a junction.

nodes.label: Untrusted Software Heuristics (implementation status)
nodes.rationale: Heuristic only; not a replacement for antivirus.

nodes.label: Testing Strategy (unit, fixture, Windows Sandbox E2E, benchmarks)
nodes.norm_label: testing strategy (unit, fixture, windows sandbox e2e, benchmarks)

nodes.label: Pull Request CI Workflow
nodes.rationale: Builds/tests only affected crates and their dependents; single ci-ok status for branch protection.

nodes.label: Release Workflow
nodes.rationale: Skips chore(release) commits to avoid recursive releases; non-cancelling concurrency group.
